activity_context.topic_title: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(A)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 6 & -3 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 13 \\ 6 & -3 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 9 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(A)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))=0.
$$
